note: The root key uses the noun’s own consonants.
summary: Genesis uses אֱמֹרִי collectively for the Amorites among Canaan’s descendants. It also applies the word to an individual member of that people.

senses.definition: A member of the Amorite people, or collectively the people as a whole.

evidence.note: The singular gentilic stands between the Jebusite and the Girgashite in the genealogy of Canaan’s descendants.
Mamre is called הָאֱמֹרִי, identifying one man as an Amorite.
The singular הָאֱמֹרִי designates the Amorites attacked at Hazazon-tamar, where הַיֹּשֵׁב says they lived.
In עֲון הָאֱמֹרִי, the singular gentilic identifies the Amorite people whose guilt is still incomplete.

senses.gloss: an Amorite or the Amorite people
